scope: User asks to draw more forward-noise inputs; bounded toy CPU comparison instead of previously proposed generated-state objective
sampling: IID joint (t,Xt) from uniform t=1,2,3 and original qref(Xt). Each initialization/stream has a pre-drawn 20x32 bank; batch sizes use nested prefixes. Independent NumPy SeedSequence([initialization,noise_stream]); no resampling based on outcomes.
inner_hard_graphs: Exactly enumerate all 64 clean-output hard graphs; only forward-noise input sampling is changed, not hard-output sampling
candidate: Same five raw-cost minimum-norm combination and same per-update old equal-weight displacement lengths as multiobjective_equalstep_cpu_20261110
exact_control: Reuse all exact-qref equal-step states/curves; exact integration has no input Monte Carlo variance but is not necessarily the best finite optimization trajectory
loss_normalization: Arithmetic average over sampled inputs; do not sum or multiply by batch size
stopping: Preserve prior rule: direction norm <=1e-12 stops affected trajectory, no invented direction or recovery. Nonfinite/KKT/state failure stops affected trajectory, save partial results. No retries, no best endpoint selection.
record: Noise bank/hash, every t/state, per-step empirical gradient error to exact gradient, exact-risk changes, step length and costs, final exact reverse distribution and full structural/diversity metrics. Separate noise-stream variation from initialization differences.
interpretation: Unbiased empirical cost gradients do not imply unbiased nonlinear MGDA direction. Equal optimizer steps are not equal exposure or compute. Toy exact input coverage was already complete; this test cannot prove more sampling repairs production models.
not_run: larger batch or longer trajectory search
